title: Smooth connected subgroup generated by a Galois-stable family of pointed affine lines
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p$ prime [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and smoothness and connectedness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ [def-sc-gm-ga] and $\mathbb A^1_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. A vector group means a $k$-group isomorphic to $\mathbf G_a^n$ for some integer $n\geq0$. Let $G$ be smooth, and fix a separable closure $K/k$ (a separably closed algebraic separable extension). Let $\mathcal F$ be any set of $K$-scheme morphisms $f:\mathbb A^1_K\to G_K$ with $f(0)=1$. Assume that $\mathcal F$ is stable under $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$, acting on the coefficients of the morphisms via the $k$-structure of $G$. There exists a unique smooth connected closed $k$-subgroup $L\subseteq G$ such that $L_K$ is the smallest closed subgroup scheme of $G_K$ through which every $f\in\mathcal F$ factors. Here smallest means that every such $f$ factors through $L_K$, and $L_K$ is contained as a closed subgroup scheme in any closed subgroup scheme through which all these morphisms factor. The empty family is allowed and gives $L=1$. Neither commutativity nor a torsion hypothesis is imposed on $G$.

source.place: Opening sentence of the proof of Theorem 2.6, printed p.12: subgroup generation by pointed affine-line images followed by Galois descent, isolated in its family form. Read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; WANTED locally. No Stacks tag is claimed for this algebraic-group result.

proof.text: Put $A_0=k[G]$ and $A=A_0\otimes_kK=k[G_K]$. For a finite subfamily $S=\{f_1,\ldots,f_r\}$ put $X_S=\mathbb A_K^{2r}$ and define $a(t)=f_1(t_1)\cdots f_r(t_r)$ and $\varphi_S(t,s)=a(t)a(s)^{-1}$. For $r=0$ use $X_S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and the unit morphism into $G_K$. This is a pointed morphism. Swapping $t,s$ inverts its value on every $K$-algebra, so its image is inverse-stable on all algebra-valued points. Setting all coordinates but $t_i$ to zero recovers $f_i$. Conversely a closed subgroup containing every $f_i$ contains $\varphi_S$, by multiplication and inversion. Thus factorization of $\varphi_S$ through a closed subgroup is equivalent to factorization of all members of $S$. For every extension $E/K$, $X_{S,E}$ has polynomial coordinate ring $E[t_1,\ldots,t_r,s_1,\ldots,s_r]$, a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]. In a domain the only idempotents are $0,1$; [lem-pc-scheme-connected-iff-idempotents] therefore gives connectedness. The same domain calculation gives reducedness. Thus $X_S$ is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected.

source.place: Propositions 2.46 and 2.48, pp.54–55; explicit inverse-stable parametrization supplied by Q45

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup] to $X_S$, its origin, and $\varphi_S$. All its hypotheses hold by step 1. It supplies the smallest closed subgroup $H_S\subseteq G_K$ containing the members of $S$, with coordinate algebra $B_S=A/I_S$, and says that $H_S$ is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected. In particular it is nonempty (it contains the identity). If $S\subseteq T$, minimality gives $H_S\subseteq H_T$ and hence $I_T\subseteq I_S$. Put $I=\bigcap_S I_S$ and $B=A/I$, the intersection indexed by all finite subfamilies, including the empty one. Write $q_S:B\to B_S$ for the quotient maps. They jointly detect zero, since an element whose lifts lie in every $I_S$ lies in $I$.

source.place: Propositions 2.46–2.51, pp.54–56; the family argument written using finite subfamilies

proof.text: The maps $q_S\otimes q_T:B\otimes_KB\to B_S\otimes_KB_T$ jointly detect zero: for fixed $T$ apply [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection] to the first factor, and then apply it to the second factor (using the symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$). In particular the diagonal maps $q_U\otimes q_U$ detect zero: the map for $(S,T)$ factors through the diagonal map for $U=S\cup T$, since $I_U\subseteq I_S\cap I_T$. Let $\Delta:A\to A\otimes_KA$ be the coordinate map of multiplication. For $b\in I$ its image in $B_U\otimes_KB_U$ under $\Delta$ is zero, because $b\in I_U$ and $H_U$ is a subgroup. The zero-detection just proved makes its image in $B\otimes_KB$ zero. Thus multiplication restricts to $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Inversion preserves each $I_S$, hence their intersection; the identity kills each $I_S$, hence $I$. The group diagrams restrict from $G_K$, so $H=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is a closed subgroup, affine of finite type as a quotient of $A$.

source.place: Proposition 2.46, pp.54–55, coordinate multiplication argument extended to families

proof.text: For every $f\in\mathcal F$, $I\subseteq I_{\{f\}}$ implies that $f$ factors through $H$. If a closed subgroup $J\subseteq G_K$ contains all $f$, then it contains every $H_S$ by step 2. Its ideal is consequently contained in every $I_S$, hence in $I$, so $H\subseteq J$. This proves the required scheme-theoretic minimality. For every field extension $E/K$, [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection] applied to $(q_S)_S$ and $N=E$ gives an injection $B\otimes_KE\to\prod_S(B_S\otimes_KE)$. Every target factor is reduced, by step 2; an element whose positive power is zero therefore maps to zero in every factor and is zero. Hence $H$ is geometrically reduced. An idempotent of $B\otimes_KE$ maps in each factor to $0$ or $1$, because $H_{S,E}$ is connected and nonempty. These values are all equal: evaluation at the common identity is the same map $B\otimes_KE\to E$ for every $S$. Injectivity now says that the original idempotent is $0$ or $1$. The identity supplies a point, so [lem-pc-scheme-connected-iff-idempotents] gives connectedness of $H_E$. Thus $H$ is geometrically connected.

source.place: Propositions 2.48, 2.51 and 2.53, pp.55–56; reducedness and idempotents for the family

proof.text: Every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ sends a smallest closed subgroup containing $\mathcal F$ to a smallest closed subgroup containing $\sigma\mathcal F$. The latter family equals $\mathcal F$ by hypothesis. Applying minimality in both directions gives $\sigma H=H$ as closed subschemes, so the defining ideal $I\subseteq A_0\otimes_kK$ of $H$ is stable under the canonical semilinear action $\sigma(a\otimes\lambda)=a\otimes\sigma(\lambda)$. A separable closure is an algebraic normal separable extension of $k$, possibly infinite. Apply [lem-sfb-galois-descent-affine-subgroups] with $J=G$, with its Galois extension taken to be $K/k$, and with $V=H$, a closed subgroup of $G_K$ by step 3. It gives a closed $k$-subgroup $L\subseteq G$ with $L_K=H$ as subgroup schemes. Write $I_0\subseteq A_0$ for the defining ideal of $L$ and $B_0=A_0/I_0$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the coordinate ring of $L_K$ is $B_0\otimes_kK$, so $L_K=H$ identifies $B_0\otimes_kK$ with $B$, compatibly with the quotient maps from $A=A_0\otimes_kK$. Finally $L$ is affine of finite type, since $B_0$ is a quotient of the finitely generated $k$-algebra $A_0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Appendix A.64–A.66, pp.580–581; Galois descent of the closed subgroup over the possibly infinite separable closure, through the existing descent node

proof.text: For the coordinate map $B_0\to B_0\otimes_kK=B$, [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] give a surjective map $H\to L$. Its source is connected by step 4, so $L$ is connected: a nontrivial clopen partition would pull back to a nontrivial clopen partition of $H$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields], choose a common overfield $\Omega$ of $K$ and an algebraic closure of $k$. By step 5, $B_0\otimes_k\Omega=B\otimes_K\Omega$, which is reduced by step 4. The map $B_0\otimes_k\bar k\to B_0\otimes_k\Omega$ is injective: in a $k$-basis of $B_0$ it is the coordinatewise inclusion of $\bar k$ in $\Omega$. This injection makes the former ring reduced. By [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-algebraic-closure-test], $L$ is geometrically reduced. Apply [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] to the finite-type group $L/k$. It is smooth, as required.

source.place: Proposition 1.26(b), p.13, and Appendix A.65, p.581; geometric reducedness after descent

proof.text: If another closed $k$-subgroup $L'$ has the stated minimality property, then $L'_K=H=L_K$ as closed subgroup schemes of $G_K$, by the two containments defining minimality. The uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-galois-descent-affine-subgroups], applied to $V=H$ (whose ideal is Galois-stable by step 5), gives $L'=L$. This proves uniqueness as a closed subgroup, not only up to isomorphism. For the empty family the identity subgroup is a closed subgroup containing all its members, and every subgroup contains it [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], so minimality gives $H=1$; then $L_K=1_K$, and the same uniqueness clause, applied to the identity subgroup of $G$, gives $L=1$. Every step used only group multiplication and inversion; no commutativity, unipotence or torsion condition was used.

source.place: Appendix A.65, p.581 (uniqueness), and Proposition 2.46, pp.54–55 (minimality)

Its statement and stmt_deps are identical to the base, where the item was unsplit with no proof. Source: Milne iAG2017 §2.h, Props 2.46–2.51 (pp.54–56), read locally; the family construction follows Milne 2.46/2.48 for families. Steps 1–4 are correct: (1) a(t)a(s)^{-1} is pointed and inverse-stable on all algebras and recovers each f_i; (2) the pointed-map node applies over K, minimality gives I_T⊆I_S, and the quotient maps jointly detect zero; (3) two applications of the tensor zero-detection lemma, with the (S,T) maps factoring through U=S∪T, test multiplication on all of H×H; (4) geometric reducedness and connectedness follow from injectivity into ∏B_S⊗E, all idempotent values agreeing with ε(e). Step 7 is also correct: connectedness through faithfully flat surjectivity, geometric reducedness through Ω ⊇ K, k̄ and the algebraic-closure test, then the Mathlib smoothness leaf with no perfectness assumption. Edge cases checked: the empty family gives L=1; t↦t^p in G_a generates G_a, not α_p; the root lines in GL_2 generate SL_2; infinite families and infinite K are handled. One fault (C5): delivered steps 5, 6 and 8 re-prove inline the existing reviewed same-unit node lem-sfb-galois-descent-affine-subgroups (unique descent of a closed subgroup with Galois-stable ideal along a possibly infinite Galois extension, equality testable after extension); the worker found only the finite-Galois node. The new step 6 (old 7) now writes out the basis injectivity.
